title: Minnesota lawyer suspended over fake AI case citations

reading.body:
The headline indicates that a lawyer in Minnesota was suspended in connection with fake case citations attributed to AI use. This pattern, seen in other documented incidents, involves a generative AI system producing plausible-looking but nonexistent legal citations, which are then submitted in legal filings without verification against actual case law databases.

The failure, if the headline accurately reflects events, would sit at the point where AI-generated output passed into a formal legal document without a human check against primary sources. Catching it would have required the lawyer, or a colleague, to verify each citation independently before filing.

What is not established is any detail about the specific AI system used, the number of citations involved, the proceedings affected, or the precise grounds and scope of the suspension, because the article body was not available for review.
